verdict_reason: A task-directory link is refused, but consult, panel, and detach still follow a linked in-repo collab root because they canonicalize it before run_dirs.
reply_markdown:
## 1
A link at `<collab>/<task>` or at `handoffs/` / `work/` is not followed. Both branches open those names with `run_dir` → `open_child` (nofollow) at `state_dir.rs:1803` and `contain.rs:198`.

Case, `..`, a trailing separator, and a different drive-letter case stay on the inside branch. `lexical` (`state_dir.rs:1863`) drops `.` and resolves `..`; `repo_relative` (`paths.rs:27`) trims a trailing separator and, on Windows, folds case (`paths.rs:14`). That match returns before `canonicalize` (`state_dir.rs:1853`). An 8.3 name that is still a string under `repo_root` does the same, and the nofollow walk then refuses the link.

Two ways still take the outside branch (`state_dir.rs:1794`) and follow a link that is the collab root or an ancestor:

- Consult, panel, and detach call `resolve_collab_root` (`providers.rs:2562`, `orchestrate/mod.rs:1516`). `canonicalize` follows a symlink or junction `.collab`, or any ancestor, and passes the target in. When that target is outside the repository, `repo_relative_normal` is `None`, and `create_dir_all` plus `Dir::open_ambient_dir` create the task there. `c3 work` joins the path and does not canonicalize (`work/mod.rs:191`), so the same link is refused.
- Inside `run_dirs`, a spelling that is not a lexical prefix — a verbatim `\\?\` path, or an 8.3 name of an ancestor that is not a prefix of `repo_root` — falls through to `canonical_prefix` (`state_dir.rs:1856`, `1901`). `canonicalize` follows links. A symlink on that path whose target lies outside selects the same outside branch.

## 2
A repository reached through a link, a worktree, and an absolute path of a real directory inside the repository still run. `resolve_repo_root` canonicalizes, `open_anchor` follows that root (`contain.rs:393`), and the walk opens real children without following them. A task directory that is itself a link is refused; the changelog names that. `c3 work` also refuses a collab directory that is a link even when the target is still inside the repository. Consult follows that link (finding 1). A cloud-sync placeholder is a reparse point and is refused; the entry counts that as a link.

## 3
Nothing wrong found on the refusal path. An existing link is not created and its target is not written; the parent already exists, so no new directory is left behind. `shown` (`state_dir.rs:2121`) names the path the walk built. The `Dir` handles are locals and drop when `run_dirs` returns. `RunStart` keeps only the move lock.

## 4
The new assertions fail on the old code: `.collab/t` (`tests.rs:923`), `.collab/t/handoffs` (`932`), a linked `.collab2` (`939`), and task `x` under an outside anchor (`958`) all `unwrap_err`. The old code followed those and returned `Ok`. The `.c3` / `.eck` refusals, both normal starts, and “the outside anchor is followed” (`952`) already held before this commit. The test calls `begin_run` on the link path and never `resolve_collab_root`, so it stays green while consult follows a linked `.collab`. If the first `dir_link` fails, the test returns at `tests.rs:868` and the new assertions never run.

The tests clause at `CHANGELOG.md:764` still says a linked task directory under `.collab/` is followed. The paragraph above and the test say it is refused.

Not read: the c3-cli tests named in the changelog, `state_dir.rs` outside `run_dirs` / `repo_relative_normal` / `folder_link_problem` / `open_write_dir`, and the cap-std Windows open implementation past `open_child`.

findings.claim: Consult, panel, and detach follow a symlink or junction used as an in-repository collab root (or as an ancestor of it) and create the task directory at the link target. resolve_collab_root canonicalizes before run_dirs, so repo_relative_normal sees the target; when that target is outside the repository the outside branch uses create_dir_all and Dir::open_ambient_dir. c3 work does not canonicalize, and the same link is refused there.
findings.trigger: The default .collab directory, or a directory on the way to it, is a symlink or junction to a directory outside the repository, and the operator runs c3 consult, a panel, or a detached run.

evidence.observation: resolve_collab_root_with ends with std::fs::canonicalize, which follows every symlink, then dunce_simplify.
build_context passes that canonical path to the Context used by begin_run and by a panel member's run_dirs.
When repo_relative_normal returns None, run_dirs create_dir_all's and open_ambient_dir's the collab path, then creates the task under that opened directory.
prepare_paths_with joins the collab path and does not canonicalize, so run_dirs still sees the in-repo link and run_dir refuses it.
The new .collab2 case calls begin_run on the link path itself and never resolve_collab_root.

findings.verification: In a scratch git repo, make .collab a symlink to an outside directory, run c3 consult with a fake reviewer, and see whether the task directory appears at the link target. Repeat with c3 work and confirm that command refuses.
findings.remedy: Decide inside versus outside on the path before following links, and open each component from the repository root with run_dir. Have resolve_collab_root leave an in-repo link for run_dirs to refuse.

findings.claim: A collab path that is inside the repository but is not a lexical prefix of repo_root is classified as outside when canonicalize follows a symlink on it. The verbatim \\?\ form, and an 8.3 short name of an ancestor that is not a string prefix of repo_root, skip the lexical match. canonical_prefix then follows the symlink, repo_relative_normal returns None, and the outside branch creates the task at the target.
findings.trigger: run_dirs is given \\?\C:\repo\.collab, or C:\Users\SHORT~1\repo\.collab, and .collab or an ancestor on that spelling is a symlink or junction to a directory outside the repository.

evidence.observation: The lexical repo_relative result is returned immediately when it matches. Only a miss calls canonical_prefix on both paths and compares those.
canonical_prefix uses std::fs::canonicalize, which follows symlinks and junctions, including the last component.
repo_relative is a string prefix. A \\?\ prefix or a different 8.3 ancestor does not match a normal repo_root even when the directory entry is inside the repo.
Drive-letter case, a trailing separator, and a lexical .. that stays under repo_root match before canonicalize, so those spellings do not select the outside branch.

findings.verification: Call run_dirs with the repo root and a \\?\ spelling of an in-repo .collab that is a symlink to an outside directory, and check whether the task directory is created at the target.
findings.remedy: Strip the verbatim prefix before the lexical test, and treat a symlink met while resolving an in-repo spelling as a refusal instead of as an outside anchor.

findings.claim: The F57-6 tests clause says the unit test still follows a linked task directory under .collab. The same entry and the test expect that link to refuse the run.
findings.trigger: A reader uses the tests clause to see what a_linked_task_directory_inside_the_folder_refuses_the_run_and_creates_nothing covers.

evidence.observation: The clause ends with “a linked task directory under .collab/ still followed”.
begin_run on .collab/t, on .collab/t/handoffs, and on a linked .collab2 is unwrap_err, and the error must name the link.

findings.verification: Read CHANGELOG.md:764 beside tests.rs:923 and confirm the clause says followed while the assertion requires an error.
findings.remedy: Replace “still followed” with the refusal the test asserts.

prior_findings.note: A task component under a real collab directory is opened nofollow in run_dir (state_dir.rs:1803), including under .c3/collab. The listed trigger is refused. A linked collab root on the consult path is a separate hole (finding 1).

unproven: No command was run. The consult follow and the \\?\ / 8.3 classification are from reading the path code.
cap-std's Windows nofollow open was taken from open_child and kind_of, not from a junction run.
The c3-cli project-folder tests named in the changelog were not read.
